thread:
sam: Heads-up RFC follow-up — we saw a couple of production incidents where clients disconnected mid-stream and the gateway kept spinning GPUs for full generation (10s of seconds). Proposing we formalize an ingress early-termination contract + backpressure negotiation so proxies can cancel/trim upstream work faster.

maria: +1 — can you sketch the contract? is this a header-level thing or a new control plane message? :thinking:

sam: Thinking header + stream-level control. Two parts: 1) client-sent hint about how tolerant it is to late tokens (a "grace window") 2) explicit resumability token so a client or frontend can request resumed work without re-running full context.

oliver: Re: "grace window" — that's tricky with streaming because generation is incremental. If client disconnects and reconnects quickly, we could keep partial KV caches for X seconds. How do we pick X?

sam: Agree. Proposal: default 5s for reconnect hot window, configurable per route. Header: `X-Resume-Hint: 5` (seconds). Gateway caches ephemeral KV and attaches `X-Resume-Token` to responses streamed so client can reattach.

nina: How does this interact with hedging / fanout? If gateway forwards same user request to two backends (hedge), we may not want to hold both GPUs after disconnect. We also need a policy for which replica owns the resume token.
sasha: Suggestion: only the winner (first sent chunk) publishes the resume token. Others abort on notification. Also gateway should expose an abort hook so we can cancel replicas ASAP: `POST /_cancel/<backend-request-id>` from the gateway to model pool.

oliver: What about cost/control plane complexity? We need to ensure cancel request cost is less than wasted compute. Canceling at the model server still blocks on current token compute. We should let runtime surface a best-effort cancellation — we send a `kill` signal, runtime responds with status `cancel_ack` and optionally `checkpoint` with last KV slot.

sam: Exactly. Example protocol sketch:

```
Client connects -> gateway -> backend(s)
Client sends: `X-Resume-Hint: 5`
Gateway streams tokens with `X-Resume-Token: tok_xyz` as trailer when it decides it's resumable
Client disconnects within 5s -> gateway keeps ephemeral cache for 5s
Client reconnects + sends `X-Resume-Token: tok_xyz` -> gateway routes to same backend if hot cache exists, else fallback to normal cold restart
```

maria: We should also define semantics for partial delivery vs. abandonment. If client doesn't reconnect, after window we should garbage-collect and emit an event to billing so we don't charge for cached state.
nina: Billing note: how to attribute cost of ephemeral cache? I'd say keep it in the original request charge; cache retention is free-within-window but if we extend beyond policy, charge storage-minutes to account. Ops can define per-customer policy.
sasha: Edge case: web clients behind flaky proxies may reconnect with different socket IPs / headers. Resume tokens must be bearer tokens with TTL; validate `X-Resume-Token` + route + optional `client-id` to avoid hijack.

oliver: Security lock: `X-Resume-Token` should be signed by gateway private key (`HMAC-SHA256`) and include expiry + route + hash(context_id). We keep verification stateless.

sam: Another tradeoff — memory footprint for KV caches. We can keep only last N layers or sub-token KV. Proposal: runtime supports a `trim_to_last_k` hint so gateway can request a lightweight cache for short windows. For long resumptions, gateway can choose to persist a fuller checkpoint to a fast store (redis/ephemeral blob).

maria: Ops/observability: need new metrics: `resume_token_issued`, `resume_hit`, `resume_miss`, `early_termination_canceled_compute_ms`, `cache_evictions`. Also tracespan for resume path.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: Can create staging deploy flag `resume-proto.v1` for canary.

sasha: Implementation responsibilities: runtime team implements cancel/trim/ack hooks + checkpoint API; gateway team implements token issuance and routing fallback; auth team reviews token format. I'll create a short RFC doc with state machine for connection lifecycle.

sam: Quick draft of connection state machine (for RFC):
```
INGRESS_STATE = {OPEN, DISCONNECTED, RESUMABLE, DRAINING, CANCELLED}
Transitions:
OPEN -> DISCONNECTED (client drops)
DISCONNECTED -> RESUMABLE (within resume_window && cache exists)
RESUMABLE -> OPEN (client reattaches with valid token)
RESUMABLE -> DRAINING (gc window expired)
ANY -> CANCELLED (explicit admin/timeout/cancel)
```

maria: Ops question: for multi-tenant Dedicated pools, should resume be enabled by default? my vote: disabled by default for Dedicated customers unless they opt-in (security + billing). Hosted free tier can have it on with short window.

oliver: Perf micro-optimization: when client disconnects, instead of full cancel we could reduce temperature/beam-size and let faster low-cost inference finish to emit closure token, then cache. Might save wasted token compute.

sam: Nice. We'll add policy knobs: `on_disconnect: [cancel, degrade, keep]` per route. Also `resume_window_seconds` and `max_cache_bytes`.

maria: Next step: sam, can you put the proto sketch + header names + state machine in the RFC doc? I'll schedule a 30m follow-up sync with runtime and gateway owners next week.

sam: On it. I'll include example headers and a tiny validation snippet: 
```
# verify resume token pseudo
payload = base64_decode(token.split(".")[0])
if hmac(payload) != token_sig: reject
if now > payload.exp: reject
```

nina: Minor: add telemetry for canceled-backend-requests so we can compute saved-GPU-seconds. That will be key to justify this feature.
sasha: Agreed. Ok let's move to RFC stage. :thumbsup:
